description: We are a team of passionate engineering students with a shared interest in technology, innovation, and space exploration. Combining our skills in programming, problem-solving, research, and creative thinking, we aim to develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges using data, science, and technology
summary:
We developed Project Cradle, an interactive, browser-based 3D space mission design and open-world planetary exploration simulator.

It directly addresses the challenge by enabling participants to cleanroom-build modular spacecraft, balance competing engineering constraints like mass, power, and financial budgets, pilot an authentic manual Sky Crane landing, and explore planetary surfaces equipped with real-time scientific telemetry.

This project is important because aerospace trade-offs and systems engineering concepts often remain abstract for students who rarely get to experiment with an entire mission from concept to operation. By gamifying authentic aerospace physics, Project Cradle bridges this gap, transforming complex engineering decision-making into an accessible, hands-on learning experience
details:
Project Details

  • What it does or how it works:Project Cradle is an interactive, browser-native 3D space mission architect and open-world planetary surveyor that guides players through an authentic end-to-end space mission lifecycle. It works through four seamless gameplay phases:

    1. 3D Cleanroom Hangar: Players assemble a modular rover or probe, balancing strict NASA "Iron Triangle" constraints—mass margins, electrical power generation, and financial budgets.
    2. Launch & Interplanetary Cruise: Executes an Earth lift-off from Cape Canaveral, stage separations, and Mars Transfer Injection (MTI).
    3. Manual Sky Crane EDL (Entry, Descent & Landing): Places the user in direct pilot control of the Powered Descent Vehicle, requiring manual retro-thruster throttling, hydrazine fuel management, and hazard avoidance for a soft touchdown ($v_y \le 2.5\text{ m/s}$).
    4. Open-World Jezero Crater Surface Ops: A 3D Martian environment where players drive a 6-wheel rover, manage solar vs. load power triage, dock with the Mars Ascent Vehicle (MAV), and deploy real NASA instruments to scan geological features.
    • Benefits: It provides a zero-install, 60 FPS experiential learning platform that runs instantly in any web browser, making aerospace systems engineering accessible to students and classrooms worldwide.
    • Intended Impact: Space systems engineering and trade-offs are traditionally taught as abstract equations with no operational consequences. Project Cradle transforms these complex compromises into engaging, high-stakes gameplay, teaching the next generation of space engineers how real mission decisions impact survival, science return, and budget efficiency.
    • Framework & Frontend: Next.js 15 (App Router), React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS for a responsive NASA JPL glass cockpit UI.
    • 3D Graphics & Shaders: Three.js and React Three Fiber (R3F) for procedural Jezero topography, PBR materials, atmospheric dust, and entry plasma effects.
    • Physics Engine: @react-three/rapier for rigid-body rover kinematics, wheel-suspension raycasts, slope traction friction, and Sky Crane tether dynamics.
    • State Management: Zustand to synchronize telemetry, MEDA weather variables, and subsystem power balances across game phases.
    • NASA Open Data: Integrated Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) HiRISE elevation data, Perseverance payload specifications, and MEDA atmospheric models.
  • How is your project creative? Instead of building a static dashboard, a basic 2D calculator, or a generic arcade driving game, Project Cradle uniquely blends hard systems engineering optimization with immersive 3D planetary exploration. By turning dry aerospace formulas (such as solar irradiance scaling and Tsiolkovsky $\Delta v$) into interactive visual mechanics—like watching your rover wheels slip on steep regolith or seeing your battery brown out during a Martian dust storm—we bridge technical accuracy with captivating game design.
    • Physical & Environmental Validity: Factored in authentic Martian constants ($g = 3.721\text{ m/s}^2$, atmospheric pressure of 757 Pa, and orbital distance solar flux scaling at 1.524 AU).
    • Operational Constraints: Considered real-world telemetry limitations, including Deep Space Network (DSN) orbital occultation windows, on-board 64 GB flash buffer constraints, and solar array dust accumulation ($\tau$ optical depth).
    • Accessibility & User Experience: Designed the entire architecture to run client-side via WebGL so judges and students can immediately launch and play via a single live web link without dependencies or installation friction.
